It appears in blockB_direct in this file and again in blockB_faithful in LiftFamilyDelB.lean. LiftFamilyDelB.lean imports this file, so the shared lemma can sit here. I did not report the following. findings.problem: The block that proves x = 1 is repeated nearly verbatim in `blockB_faithful` in LiftFamilyDelB.lean, which imports this file. Both proofs show ⊤ ≤ ker(x - id) by rewriting with ← V_sum and applying sup_le (iSup_le …). They split the index k as k = i or k ≠ i. In the case k = i they use the hypothesis that x fixes commGL (Lc i) ⊤. In the case k ≠ i they use blockB_le_centSub_I, and on fixGL (oddGen H) they use blockB_le_centSub_C. Both finish with LinearEquiv.ext. This is a multi-step argument about the module decomposition, not a routine unfolding, and it is maintained in two places. The only difference is that blockB_direct derives the fixing hypothesis from the supremum over the other blocks, while blockB_faithful takes it as an assumption.
findings.proposed_change: Move `blockB_faithful` (statement: `(ctx : FamilyCtx H T n F r Lc) (i : Fin r) {b : V ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] V} (hb : b ∈ blockB H (Lc i)) (h : ∀ u ∈ commGL (Lc i) ⊤, b u = u) : b = 1`) into this file, just before `blockB_direct`, with the proof it already has. Delete the copy in LiftFamilyDelB.lean. Callers there keep working because the file imports this one and uses the same namespace. Then `blockB_direct` keeps its `hfixI` step and ends with `exact Subgroup.mem_bot.2 (blockB_faithful ctx i hxi fun u hu => hfixI u hu)`. This removes the `hall` block (about 17 lines, lines 182–199). Its hypotheses and imports are unchanged, because `blockB_faithful` needs only `V_sum`, `blockB_le_centSub_I` and `blockB_le_centSub_C`, all available here.
findings.benefit: The V_sum decomposition argument for blocks lives in one named lemma instead of two copies. `blockB_direct` shrinks to its mathematical content: the other blocks fix commGL (Lc i) ⊤, so the intersection is trivial. Later changes to the block-fixing lemmas or to V_sum then need one edit, not two.
